sections.heading: 1. Electric Current, Charge and Potential
points: **Electric current (I)** = rate of flow of charge; I = Q/t; unit **ampere (A)** (1 A = 1 coulomb/second); measured by an **ammeter (in series)**.
Conventional current flows opposite to electron flow.
**Potential difference (V)** = work done per unit charge; unit **volt (V)** (1 V = 1 J/C); measured by a **voltmeter (in parallel)**.
A **cell/battery** maintains the potential difference that drives current.

sections.heading: 2. Ohm's Law and Resistance
points: **Ohm's Law:** V = IR (current ∝ potential difference at constant temperature).
**Resistance (R)** opposes current; unit **ohm (Ω)**.
R depends on: **length (R ∝ l)**, **area (R ∝ 1/A)**, **material (resistivity ρ)** and temperature; R = ρl/A.
**Resistivity (ρ)** — property of material; metals/alloys have low ρ (conductors); insulators high. Alloys (nichrome) have higher resistivity → used in heating elements.

sections.heading: 3. Combination of Resistors
points: **Series:** same current; total R = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ (adds up, larger); voltage divides.
**Parallel:** same voltage; 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ (total R smaller than smallest); current divides.
**Household wiring** uses **parallel** connection (each appliance gets full voltage, works independently).

sections.heading: 4. Heating Effect and Electric Power
points: **Joule's law of heating:** H = I²Rt — heat produced ∝ I², R, and time.
Applications: **electric heater, iron, geyser, electric bulb (filament of tungsten), fuse** (protects circuit — melts on excess current).
**Electric power (P)** = VI = I²R = V²/R; unit **watt (W)**; 1 kW = 1000 W.
**Commercial unit of energy = kilowatt-hour (kWh) = 1 'unit'**; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Current = ampere (ammeter in series); potential difference = volt (voltmeter in parallel).
Ohm's law: V = IR; resistance unit = ohm; R = ρl/A.
Series: R adds up; Parallel: 1/R adds up (household wiring = parallel).
Joule's heating: H = I²Rt; fuse protects circuit.
Power P = VI; commercial energy unit = kWh (1 unit) = 3.6×10⁶ J.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel**.
**Series resistance adds up; parallel gives smaller total** (1/R = Σ1/Rᵢ).
**Household wiring is in parallel** (full voltage, independent operation).
**1 unit of electricity = 1 kilowatt-hour** (not 1 kilowatt).
